newsitem.title: CANADA: Azcar shares rise on U.S. FCC ruling.
newsitem.headline: Azcar shares rise on U.S. FCC ruling.

text.p: Shares in engineering firm Azcar Technologies Inc rose in active trade on Friday after a U.S. Federal Communications Commission ruling deemed likely to create business for the company, an analyst said.
Azcar builds television broadcast studios and has a number of major U.S. clients including satellite broadcasting company EchoStar, said John Grandy, an analyst at Deacon Capital Corp.
The stock rose 0.70 to 4.00 in turnover of 630,950 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. It was still trading below its 52-week high of 4.35.
"The reason why (the stock) is interesting is that yesterday the U.S. Federal Communications Commission adopted a new policy for the introduction of digital tv broadcasting in the U.S.," Grandy said.
"It basically said within nine years, the entire industry is going to have to convert from the current broadcast standard, which is analog, to digital," he added.
Under pressure from FCC officials, 23 stations have pledged to initiate broadcasts in the top 10 markets within 18 months.
"So this creates a great opportunity for Azcar Technologies. They do business in both Canada and the States but most of it is in the States," Grandy said.
